text:
Required Documents for Hypothecation (HP) Termination: -
If you are visiting this RTO for Hypothecation removal, here is the exact checklist of documents you need. Save yourself time and money by prepping these in advance:

Apply Online First 💻
Before you even head to the RTO, you must submit the Hypothecation Termination application online via the Parivahan portal and pay the required fee. You cannot just walk in with bank papers.

1. Original RC:  Keep the original card ready, and bring a transparent plastic pouch/cover to attach the card to your file.
2. Fee Receipt: Bring a (B/W) printout of your online RTO fee payment.
3. NOC & Form 35 (Crucial Step): Must be a Colour printout only.
Real Tip: If your bank/loan provider (like Bajaj) gave you a digitally signed and sealed Form 35, it is 100% valid. Local third-party agents might try to tell you that you need a physical stamp and ink signature to scare you into using their services. Don't listen to them; digital works perfectly.
4. Latest Emission Certificate:  Bring a B/W printout (ensure it hasn't expired).
5. Valid Insurance Policy: Bring a B/W printout of your active policy.
6. DL & RC Copies: Bring a B/W photocopy of both your Driving Licence and your current Registration Certificate.
💡 Pro-Tips for a Smooth Visit:
-> File Folder: Everything needs to be submitted in a standard paper file tag folder. You don't need to bring one from home; you can easily buy a paper file at any nearby Xerox shop right outside the RTO.
* Organize your documents in the exact order listed above before reaching the counter to save time!
note: warns that local agents give wrong advice; a how-to, not an experience

Went for my driving test at Jnanabharathi RTO, and honestly, what a complete mess. Not sure if this is the same as Ullal RTO, but Jayanagar tests are also done here.
First off, this RTO is supposedly for Jayanagar but it’s almost 10 km. Already a pain just getting here.

When I reached, literally everyone there was with agents. I had my helmet, ready to take the test, and I’d read online that sometimes agents provide a vehicle for ₹200–₹300, since I didn't have one. Asked an agent, he straight up laughed at me and said, “haha where’s your vehicle? you have a helmet but no vehicle?” like I was some kind of joke. These agents reject you worse than a hot chick would.

Then inside the office, the guy taking photos asks me “which agent?” I said I don’t have one. Immediately his tone changes and he tells me to provide vehicle documents. I explain I don’t have a vehicle and will try asking someone outside. He bluntly says, “then you can’t take the test.”
So I ask 3–4 agents outside if they can provide a vehicle—none of them allow it. Basically, if you didn’t come through an agent from the start, you’re treated like you shouldn’t even be there.

And the funniest part? Everyone knows how this place works. If you go via an agent, you barely even give the test. Bikes? Partial ride and you’re passed. Cars? Agent sits next to you, it’s rigged. Nobody cares about the actual test — all they care about is getting their cut.

This is honestly the perfect example of how the Indian system works—and will continue to work. These people aren’t so-called government servants—they treat us like servants, as if we’re begging to get our work done for free.

Moral of the story? Leave the country asap. Don’t waste your time or dignity here. Absolute garbage system run by money-minded people.

I had a very frustrating experience with the Devanahalli RTO while renewing the registration of my bike.

An agent first quoted me ₹8,500 for the FC/registration renewal. I decided to do it myself, and the actual government fee came to only ₹3,912. So if you’re willing to spend some time, you can save a lot of money.

I submitted all my documents and paid the fees on 10th April. The inspection was completed on 13th April, and I was called again on 16th April to collect the documents. At that time, I specifically asked whether I needed to come back again. The staff told me, “Everything is completed. You’ll receive your RC Smart Card within 45 days.

I waited for more than 60 days, but nothing happened. Finally, I visited the office on 2nd July, after 77 days and only after I asked about my application did they take my file from the cupboard and process it further. I was then told that I would receive my RC within 10 days.

Later, I checked the Parivahan portal, which showed that my RC was printed on 9th July and dispatch was generated on 14th July. Even after waiting, I still didn’t receive it.

So on 22nd July, I went to the RTO again. The notice board clearly says lunch break is from 1:30 PM to 2:15 PM, but the concerned person came only around 3:15 PM. During that one hour, I saw several people come looking for him, see the empty counter, and leave without getting any help.

When he finally checked, my RC Smart Card was still lying in their office. I was told it had been returned because my address was “invalid.” But when I checked the address on the document, it was completely correct. Then I was asked to pay the return charge. I refused because I had already made multiple unnecessary visits due to the delay. After that, they finally handed over my RC card.
The most disappointing part wasn’t the fee it was the lack of responsibility and communication. If I hadn’t kept following up myself, I honestly don’t know how much longer my RC would have remained there.

Most of the time, the chairs were empty, and the concerned staff were nowhere to be found. I saw many people come to the counter, wait for a while, realize no one was available to assist them, and then leave without getting their work done.

I hope the department improves its service, processes applications on time, and respects people’s time. Citizens shouldn’t have to make repeated visits for work that should have been completed months earlier.

While online application process is simple enough on Vahan portal, I personally did not find any sense for offline application submission since application is already submitted online to the department and they have all the details already in there database.

Old RC should be received via courier service and within committed time new RC should be delivered back to the citizens (some additional 5-10 days is understood but not indefinite delays). I don't see a sense why I should spend 2000 bucks on commute, waste fuel (super important), add more to already chaotic traffic and pollution, and most importantly waste my 10 hours of unnecessary hassle in traffic.

Adapt better practices and let citizens also breathe :)

text: 1st time in my life, i got my driving license done without and bribe !! I had not expected this in my lifetime, but i am indebted to Parivahan/Sarathi/MORTH and central/state governments for making this happen (though this is kind of expected given that i pay lakhs in income tax over years and lakhs in vehicle registrations over years, but expectations never met reality so far). Since my DL was already from KA53 RTO, i had gone last time and bribed an agent to get the process done. This time i was ambitious and read the online procedure and decided to apply online, got all the paperwork but needed medical fitness certificate. So, i took the filled certificate printout online and went to local PHC and am really thankful to the Doctor and staff to sign it without any hassles (even more professional than private ones). So, all my procedure completed online and got a note "no need to visit RTO, fully online" - happily i waited for 2-3 weeks and no status changed, which got me worried, also there was a note online for document check in room #2. So off i went to the RTO and front office staff guided me to upper floor without language barriers and on 1st floor staff confirmed that this is fully online, no need to visit - delay is because of ongoing survey that has pulled the staff for survey duty. I waited for a month more and was surprised to see it updated and approved. After a few days got an sms that DL is dispatched by India Post with a tracking number. The tracking number did not get updated on India Post website, but there was a note that there may be some gap between tracking number available vs actual item being handed over. Finally about 10 days after the SMS, i checked to see that my DL reached local SO and postman delivered it to home. Such a proud feeling to finally get my DL without paying any bribe. Jai ho !!
note: praise is for the online process and a clinic, not clearly this office
